text: 23. This microscopic creature usually resides within the galls of oak trees, where it feeds on other developing insects. During the summer and fall, large numbers of them can drift down from the trees and land unnoticed on people below. Their bites inject a toxin that causes a distinctive skin reaction, though the symptoms usually don't appear until 10 to 16 hours later. Name this mite.

24. These larval mites are nearly invisible and are commonly encountered in areas of tall grass or brush. Contrary to popular belief, they do not burrow under the skin; instead, they attach to the surface and inject enzymes that dissolve skin cells. This process creates a hardened feeding tube called a "stylostome," which results in the incredibly itchy red welts they are famous for. Identify them.
